brief.outcome: Fewer clinics cancel in their first three months, so overall monthly churn falls from 6.5% to under 4% within two quarters, without a price change.

ambition.goal_beyond: A larger base of clinics that stay past month three, so every new signup adds to the base instead of replacing a leaver.
rungs: Rewrite the onboarding emails and in-app messages that go out today and ship them.
Find which clinics leave early and why from the raw billing, usage and support records, then fix the biggest causes in onboarding, emails and in-app messages.
Do rung 2 as a holdout test, then keep a weekly check that flags new clinics stalling before month three, so early churn stays down without being asked.
ambition.judge: Stripe cancellations by signup cohort, treated clinics against a randomised holdout, read from Stripe's own records and not from our working tables.

brief.deliverable: Changed onboarding, emails and in-app messages launched to new clinics with your approval and a holdout group, a weekly early-warning list, and an honest readout against the 4% target.

answers.question: What business and how big?
answers.answer: B2B scheduling software for clinics, about 900 paying accounts, $79 a month per account.

answers.question: What is churn now and where is it?
answers.answer: 6.5% overall monthly churn. The owner believes most of it is in months one to three (Stripe dashboard).

answers.question: Which tools can your AI reach?
answers.answer: Mixpanel and Intercom have MCP read access. Stripe is read-only.

answers.question: Do you know why they cancel?
answers.answer: No cancellation survey. Unknown: whether clinics churn because of a missing integration.

answers.question: What is the target and by when?
answers.answer: Overall monthly churn under 4% within two quarters.

answers.question: What can we change?
answers.answer: Onboarding, emails and in-app messages. Not pricing this year.

answers.question: Who decides?
answers.answer: The owner with the head of product.

research.approach: Practitioners do not treat a blended churn rate as one problem. They rebuild churn from the raw subscription records, split it by how long the account had been paying (the hazard by tenure month) and by chosen cancellation versus failed payment, and only then ask why. The early-months spike is usually accounts that never reached first value, so they join billing to product events and support conversations per account, find the early behaviour that separates stayers from leavers, and read the leavers' own words. Fixes go out as a controlled test with a randomised holdout, scored on cancellations from the billing system, not on opens or clicks. A weekly check flags new accounts that stall before the risky months.

sources.title: Subscriber cohorts and cohort retention in Billing (Stripe Support)
sources.note: Stripe puts subscribers in cohorts by the month they first pay and checks each month, in UTC, whether they churned; a re-subscriber stays in the original cohort. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Cancel subscriptions (Stripe Docs)
sources.note: Subscriptions cancel automatically after up to eight failed billing attempts, so some cancellations are not a clinic's choice. Cancelled subscriptions keep a cancellation_details field. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Add a cancellation page to the customer portal (Stripe Docs)
sources.note: Stripe can ask for a cancellation reason from a fixed list and shows it on the subscription, in Sigma and in the subscription webhook. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Automate payment retries: Smart Retries (Stripe Docs)
sources.note: Stripe's own tool for retrying failed payments to prevent involuntary churn; set in Billing, Revenue recovery. Seen in search results, not opened in full. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Retention report (Mixpanel Docs)
sources.note: Retention is set by an initial event and a return event, with rolling or calendar windows and breakdowns; the same pages build cohorts from behaviour. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

sources.title: Track and understand the topics your customers chat about (Intercom Help)
sources.note: Conversation topics can be applied retroactively to old conversations, are in the conversations export and the API, and split reports. Topics do not record when they were added.

sources.title: The churn hazard curve: why one churn rate hides three different problems (Koji)
sources.note: Divide churners in a tenure month by accounts that entered it still active. Early months (about 0 to 3) are a different problem from mid-life and late churn. Warns about averaging across them and mistaking sorting for loyalty. Vendor write-up, updated 2026-09-29.

sources.title: Holdout campaign (Agile Brand Guide)
sources.note: Withhold a predefined share (5 to 20% depending on traffic and effect) of the eligible audience, randomise at the level of exposure, size by power analysis, analyse as intention to treat, audit delivery logs for leaks. No date on the page; accessed 2026-11-03.

steps.name: Rebuild churn from raw Stripe records, split chosen from failed-payment
steps.why: The dashboard figure is a report until rebuilt; failed payments need a different fix from a clinic choosing to leave.

steps.name: Plot churn by tenure month, not one blended rate
steps.why: It confirms or refutes the belief that churn sits in months one to three and shows whether it is one problem or several.

steps.name: Join billing, usage and support per account and check the join
steps.why: Usage and support evidence only helps if each account matches across the three systems.

steps.name: Find the early behaviour that separates stayers from leavers
steps.why: Early churn is usually accounts that never reached first value; the activation event has to come from the data.

steps.name: Read the leavers' own words in support, and start capturing a reason
steps.why: There is no cancellation survey; support text is the only voice of leavers, and the missing-integration question lives there.

steps.name: Change onboarding, emails and in-app messages around the milestone
steps.why: These are the levers the owner allows; each should fire on what a clinic has or has not done.

steps.name: Launch as a randomised holdout test scored on cancellations
steps.why: Without a holdout, a change cannot be told from the season or from sorting.

steps.name: Keep a weekly early-warning list of stalled new clinics
steps.why: It keeps early churn down after the test without waiting for the next problem.

steps.name: Offer a retention coupon or discount at cancel
steps.why: A common save tactic at the cancel step.

pitfalls.text: Treating one blended churn rate as one problem; early, mid-life and late churn have different causes.
Counting failed-payment cancellations as clinics choosing to leave, then fixing the wrong thing.
Reading a flattening curve as loyalty when high-risk accounts simply left first.
Counting very recent signups as retained before they have had 90 days.
Picking the activation event by correlation alone, when stayers may just be better-fit clinics; only a holdout shows it causes retention.
Holdout accounts still receiving the new messages through another tool, or judging the test on opens instead of cancellations.

stages.name: Pin down the problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Rebuild churn from Stripe records
stages.goal: Load the raw subscription and invoice history into the Postgres schema and rebuild monthly churn, churn by tenure month and each cancellation as chosen or failed payment.

outputs.name: What was pulled, definitions and the rebuilt churn

checks.name: Rebuilt overall monthly churn is within 0.3 percentage points of the reported 6.5%, or the definition gap is written down
Churn by tenure month is divided by accounts that entered the month still active, and signups under 90 days old are marked immature
At least 95% of cancellations are classified as chosen or failed payment, using cancellation_details and invoice history

stages.name: Gather usage, support and current messages
stages.goal: Pull first-90-day product events and support conversations for every account in the same period as the billing history, plus the messages sent today.

outputs.name: What was pulled and the gaps

checks.name: Events and conversations cover the same dates as the billing history
All pulls were read-only and nothing was sent to a clinic
Any missing event, tool or period is named in the notes

stages.name: Check the join can be trusted
stages.goal: Check accounts match across Stripe, Mixpanel and Intercom and that the events used to judge activation actually fire, before anyone reasons from them.

checks.name: At least 95% of paying accounts match by id between Stripe and Mixpanel, and the unmatched are listed
Each query joins at one row per account and its counts match the source within 1%
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the diagnosis

stages.name: Find who leaves early and why
stages.goal: Test the hypotheses on the checked data: churn by tenure, chosen against failed payment, the activation milestone, support themes including integration requests, and today's messages. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with the numbers behind it
Each retention claim is checked by signup month to rule out sorting, and signups under 90 days old are excluded or marked
Each main finding names a competing explanation, and activation is called a correlation until the holdout shows it
Any segment with fewer than 30 cancellations is marked low-confidence

stages.name: Rank what to change
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked cards limited to onboarding, emails and in-app messages; send anything outside those limits, such as an integration, to the head of product as a finding.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected direction, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured in Stripe cancellations
No card changes price or discounts, and any card outside onboarding, emails and in-app messages is marked as a finding for product

stages.name: Owner and head of product choose
stages.goal: Pick card ids. Ask for the reason when the top card is passed over, and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are in decisions.jsonl

stages.name: Write the onboarding, email and in-app changes
stages.goal: Write the chosen changes so each message fires on what a clinic has or has not done and stops once it has done it, plus the stalled-account rule for the weekly list.

outputs.name: Messages with trigger, timing and exit rule

checks.name: Every change traces to a chosen card
Every message names the clinic action that triggers it and the action that stops it
No message mentions a price change or discount, and plain wording is at grade 8 to 10 reading level

stages.optional_when: No onboarding, email or in-app card was chosen.

stages.name: Design the holdout test
stages.goal: Fix who gets the changes: eligible clinics in their first 90 days, randomly assigned by account in the Postgres schema, with a holdout, a sample size and a stop rule.

checks.name: Assignment is random by account, reproducible with a stored seed, and the two groups match on signup month within 5 points
Sample size and holdout share (between 5 and 20%) come from a power calculation on real signup counts, or the stage says what is missing
The primary measure is cancellation in Stripe by day 90, analysed as intention to treat

stages.name: Ship the changes to the test group
stages.goal: Register the experiment, freeze the assignment, then the owner switches on each approved message for the test group only and we read back what was sent.

checks.name: The experiment and frozen assignment are in experiments.jsonl before the first message is sent
Delivery logs show zero new messages sent to holdout accounts
Each shipped message was read back from the tool and matches the approved text

stages.name: Read results against Stripe
stages.goal: Compare treated and holdout clinics on cancellation in Stripe, track overall monthly churn against the 4% target, and keep the weekly list of stalled new clinics. Read-only.

checks.name: Churn figures are recomputed from Stripe's own cohort retention records, not from our working tables, and agree within 0.3 points
A verdict is given only when the planned sample is reached, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE with the confidence range

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close the experiment, save rules with their scope, hand the head of product any integration finding, and plan the next round.

hypotheses.statement: Most cancellations happen in the first three months of paying.
hypotheses.test: Churn by tenure month from raw Stripe records, dividing by accounts that entered each month still active, over the last 12 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Months 1 to 3 hold more than 50% of cancellations and their monthly hazard is at least twice the hazard of months 7 to 12.
hypotheses.refute_if: Months 1 to 3 hold under 35% of cancellations, or the hazard is flat across tenure.

hypotheses.statement: A material share of early cancellations are failed payments, not a clinic's choice.
hypotheses.test: Classify each cancellation by cancellation_details and invoice history (payment failed and retries ran out versus cancelled by the customer).
hypotheses.confirm_if: Failed payments are 20% or more of cancellations in months 1 to 3.
hypotheses.refute_if: Failed payments are under 10% of cancellations in months 1 to 3.

hypotheses.statement: Early leavers never reached first value.
hypotheses.test: Pick candidate activation events from Mixpanel and compare the share of leavers and stayers that did each within 14 days of paying; check by signup month.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 60% of early leavers never did the event, against at most 30% of stayers, and the gap holds in each signup month.
hypotheses.refute_if: Leavers and stayers differ by under 10 points, or the gap disappears within signup months.

hypotheses.statement: Clinics that reach first value late leave more than those that reach it fast.
hypotheses.test: Days from first payment to the activation event; churn by 90 days for those under 7 days against 14 days or more.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Churn is at least 1.5 times higher for those at 14 days or more, with at least 30 accounts per group.
hypotheses.refute_if: Churn is within 20% across timing groups.

hypotheses.statement: Early leavers cancel because of a missing integration.
hypotheses.test: Tag Intercom conversations and topics of early leavers for integration, import or sync requests before they cancelled, and compare with stayers.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 15% of early leavers raised an integration need and the rate is at least twice that of stayers.
hypotheses.refute_if: Under 5% of early leavers did, and the rate is no higher than for stayers.

hypotheses.statement: Early leavers hit slow or unresolved help in their first 30 days.
hypotheses.test: First response time and share of conversations left unresolved in the first 30 days, leavers against stayers.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Leavers' unresolved share is at least twice the stayers' and their median first response is longer.
hypotheses.refute_if: The two groups are within 20% on both measures.

hypotheses.statement: Today's messages run on a timer and ignore what the clinic has done.
hypotheses.test: List each current email and in-app message with its trigger and timing and compare with each clinic's activation progress.
hypotheses.confirm_if: No message depends on a missed milestone, or stalled clinics get the same messages as active ones.
hypotheses.refute_if: Messages already branch on milestones and stalled clinics receive different ones.

hypotheses.statement: Recent signup cohorts leave faster than older ones, for example after an acquisition or product change.
hypotheses.test: Compare day-90 survival for the last three signup months against the three before them.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Survival is at least 5 points lower for the recent cohorts.

dropped.reason: A retention coupon at cancel is a price change, which the owner ruled out for this year, and Stripe is read-only for us.

measurement.window: First look when treated clinics reach day 30; verdict when they reach day 90; overall monthly churn read every month against 4%.
measurement.min_volume: Set by the power calculation on the real signup count (not yet known); for scale, 900 accounts at 6.5% is about 58 cancellations a month overall (derived from the owner's figures).
measurement.stop_rule: Stop early only if a guardrail breaks, such as support conversations per new clinic rising or a message firing at the wrong clinics; otherwise run to day 90 before a verdict.
